svg.aria-label: How to read a shadow report. The report shows a difference rate and lists differences field by field at component level. One row says PID-5.1 differs on 12 messages, live produced SMITH and candidate produced Smith, a single mapping decision. Another says a filter disagreement where the live channel kept a message the candidate dropped, counted on its own because it decides whether a receiving system hears about a patient. Timestamps and control IDs such as MSH-7 and MSH-10 are ignored as expected differences. When everything matches, the report says the candidate changed nothing on the traffic seen so far.
svg.title: Reading a shadow report, field by field
svg.text: What the Shadow tab tells you
over the real traffic seen so far
reported at component level, so you see exactly which piece changed
live produced "SMITH" · candidate produced "Smith" — one mapping decision
the live channel kept a message the candidate dropped
counted on its own: it decides whether a receiving system hears about a patient at all
timestamps and control IDs change on every message — MSH-7 and MSH-10 are the common pair to ignore
When everything matches, the report says so plainly: the candidate changed nothing on the traffic seen so far.
That is evidence you can act on — not a single pass-or-fail, but a list of real changes, each one click from the message that caused it.
